headline: The Physical Therapy Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet patients, give numbers and times, describe pain and swelling, ask simple questions, give polite exercise instructions and ask for help, and start Physical Therapy Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet a patient, say who you are, and pronounce the body parts you work with every day.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent; greetings with patients

words.note: ll sounds like English y: ro-DEE-ya; the r at the start is trilled.
The h is always silent: OHM-bro.
Every vowel is short and clear: es-PAL-da.
A single r between vowels is a quick tap, like the dd in ladder.
ll like y: to-BEE-yo.
ue sounds like way: KWAY-yo.
ch sounds as in church.
j sounds like a strong English h: eh-hehr-SEE-syo.
rr is a strong trill; the single r in paralelas is a tap.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: MOOS-koo-lo.
Terapeuta is the same for a man or a woman.
Use señor for a man.
Formal: use usted with patients.

words.en: See you at the next appointment.
words.es: Nos vemos en la próxima cita.

lessons.speaking: Greet a patient, say your name and that you are their therapist, then point to the knee, hip and shoulder and say each word clearly.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give appointment times, sets, repetitions, pounds and degrees to a patient.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and sets, reps, seconds, pounds, feet and degrees

words.note: 3 series de 10 means 3 sets of 10.
Range of motion is measured in degrees.
US clinics measure weights in pounds.
The hand weight or dumbbell.
Plural veces: 2 veces al día means twice a day.

words.en: According to your program, it's 3 sets of 10 repetitions.
words.es: Según su programa, son 3 series de 10 repeticiones.

words.note: Use es a las for the time of an event.
Use de with a measurement.

words.en: Today you bend your knee to 90 degrees.
words.es: Hoy usted dobla la rodilla hasta 90 grados.

words.note: Pies means feet for distance, the same word as the body part.

words.en: According to the doctor's order, therapy is 3 times a week.
words.es: Según la orden del médico, la terapia es 3 veces por semana.

lessons.speaking: Tell a patient what time their next appointment is, how many sets and repetitions are in their program, and how many pounds the weight is.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe how a patient feels and where things are in the clinic with ser and estar.
lessons.focus: ser for what someone or something is, estar for a patient's condition or a location

words.note: Agrees with the noun: la rodilla está hinchada.
Use with estar: estoy adolorido, or adolorida for a woman.
Say cansada to or about a woman.
estar listo means ready; ser listo means smart.
ser for a profession; the same word for a man or a woman.
estar: a condition that can change.
Ask ¿Está mareada? to a woman.

words.en: The gym is on the second floor.
words.es: El gimnasio está en el segundo piso.
words.note: estar for location.

words.es: Usted está más fuerte esta semana.

lessons.speaking: Ask a patient how they feel today, describe their knee as swollen, stiff or strong, and tell them where the therapy gym is.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what equipment there is, what a patient needs or wants, and what has to be done.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive with clinic equipment

words.note: Common in Mexico; you will also hear el andador.
Follow your clinic's protocol for time on the skin.

words.en: You need the walker to walk.
Do you want ice after the exercise?
You have to walk with the walker.
words.es: Hay que caminar con la andadera.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: a general must, without naming who.

words.en: I have a resistance band for you.
words.es: Tengo una banda elástica para usted.

lessons.speaking: Tell a patient what equipment there is in the gym, ask if they want ice or a hot pack, and say they need the walker.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Tell a patient today's plan and ask what they can do at home.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, and poder for what a patient can do

words.note: US and Mexico; el coche in Spain.
Mexico; la ducha in other countries.
Without an article it means tomorrow; la mañana is the morning.

words.en: Let's go to the hallway to walk.
words.note: a + el = al.

words.en: Today we're going to do exercises for the hip.
words.es: Hoy vamos a hacer ejercicios para la cadera.

words.en: You're going to do these exercises at home.
words.es: Usted va a hacer estos ejercicios en casa.

words.en: Tomorrow we're going to walk more.
Can you go up the stairs?
Can you get in and out of the car?

lessons.speaking: Tell a patient what you are going to do today, then ask if they can climb the stairs, use the shower and get into the car at home.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Talk about a patient's daily routine and your own work with present-tense verbs.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Feminine even though it ends in -o.
Also toes: los dedos del pie.
Feminine noun that takes el: el agua fría.
Mexico; por la noche in other countries.

words.en: Are you working in the gym tomorrow?
words.note: Informal tú, to a coworker.

words.en: Do you live alone or with your family?
words.es: ¿Usted vive solo o con su familia?
words.note: Say sola to a woman.

lessons.speaking: Ask a patient if they live alone and walk every day, then ask a coworker if they work in the gym tomorrow.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask a patient simple questions about their pain, surgery and help at home.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál in patient questions

words.note: Agrees with the noun: cuánto dolor, cuántas veces.
Two words for why; porque (one word) means because.
Use it for a choice between things.
la médica or la doctora for a woman.

words.en: From 0 to 10, how much pain do you have?

words.note: Use la instead of lo with a woman.

words.en: Which one hurts more, the right or the left?
words.es: ¿Cuál le duele más, la derecha o la izquierda?

words.en: What activity is hard for you?

lessons.speaking: Ask a patient where it hurts, how much pain they have from 0 to 10, when their surgery was, and who helps them at home.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Use negatives and more or less to check feeling, limits and progress with a patient.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro in therapy talk

words.note: Before the verb: nunca camine; after it, add no: no camine nunca.
After the verb, add no: no hay nadie.
Never with un: say otro ejercicio.

words.en: For now, never walk without the walker.
words.es: Por ahora, nunca camine sin la andadera.

words.en: Is there nobody at home with you?
words.es: ¿No hay nadie en casa con usted?

words.en: Don't you feel anything in your foot?
According to your doctor, you can't drive yet.
words.es: Según su médico, todavía no puede manejar.

words.en: Today the knee is less swollen.
words.es: Hoy la rodilla está menos hinchada.

lessons.speaking: Tell a patient to do the exercise on the other side, ask if they feel nothing in the foot, and say their doctor says they cannot drive yet.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Give a patient polite, clear instructions to move, sit, stand and breathe.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands: siéntese, párese, doble, apriete, respire

words.note: Lying on your back.
Lying on your stomach.
Here it means straight; for the right side say la derecha.

words.en: Can you lie on your back, please?
words.note: ¿Puede + infinitive? is softer than a command.

words.en: Sit on the edge of the bed.
words.es: Siéntese en la orilla de la cama.

words.en: Stand up and hold the walker.
words.note: Mexico: párese means stand up; levántese also works.

words.en: Breathe normally, don't hold your breath.
words.es: Respire normal, no aguante el aire.

lessons.speaking: Guide a patient from the bed to standing: ask them to sit on the edge, stand up, hold the walker and breathe normally.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize therapy cognates and use survival phrases when you don't understand a patient.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad, -ente, and phrases for asking for help

words.note: -ción words are feminine: la evaluación.
-dad words are feminine: la actividad.
la paciente for a woman.
-ente adjectives are the same for a man or a woman.

words.en: How do you say this in Spanish?
I'm going to call an interpreter.
words.es: Voy a llamar a un intérprete.
words.note: Use the personal a before a person: llamar a.

lessons.speaking: Tell a patient you don't understand, ask them to repeat more slowly, and say you are going to call an interpreter.
